title: F90 array section A(2:N:2) — strided slice; passing to a routine creates a contiguous-or-non-contiguous decision
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE PROCESS_EVEN(A, N)
C     A(2:N:2) is the array section containing A(2), A(4), A(6)...
C     If the called routine expects a contiguous array (legacy F77
C     style), the compiler MAY copy the section into a temp buffer
C     before the call and copy it back after -- a 'copy-in copy-out'
C     pattern. Mutating the formal arg during the call may not
C     visibly mutate the caller's A until after RETURN.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER N
      REAL    A(:)
      CALL DOUBLE_ALL(A(2:N:2))
      END
notes: F90 array sections (A(L:U:S)) are a major source of port surprise. A Java/C# rewrite that passes a 'view' (e.g. via index arithmetic) doesn't match the F90 copy-in-copy-out semantics. The spec must flag whether the section is passed to a subroutine and surface the read-vs-mutate question.
